Interactive charts: clicks in shiny

Source: vignettes/click-events.Rmd
click-events.Rmd

In a shiny app or an rvis dashboard, a click on an item of a chart (a node or link of a graph, a bar, a point, a slice, a table cell or a map marker) can set a shiny input, so that other outputs react to it: show the details of the clicked node, filter a table by the clicked bar, zoom a map.

rvisClickEvents() adds this to a chart. It adds a small javascript function to the htmlwidget with htmlwidgets::onRender(), which runs after the plotting package has drawn the chart: the javascript of the plotting package is not copied or changed, so new versions of the package keep working.

In a shiny app

Wrap the chart in rvisClickEvents(). A click then sets input$<output id>_item_click:

library(shiny)
library(rvis)

ui <- fluidPage(
  echarts4r::echarts4rOutput("bars"),
  verbatimTextOutput("clicked"))

server <- function(input, output) {
  output$bars <- echarts4r::renderEcharts4r({
    deaths <- data.frame(age = rownames(VADeaths), VADeaths, check.names = FALSE)
    rvisClickEvents(rvisPlot("bar", "echarts", obj = deaths, x = "age", y = list("Rural Male", "Urban Male")))
  })
  output$clicked <- renderPrint(str(input$bars_item_click))
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

A click on the 70-74 bar of the Rural Male series gives:

List of 9
 $ type  : chr "point"
 $ id    : chr "70-74"
 $ label : chr "70-74"
 $ series: chr "Rural Male"
 $ index : int 4
 $ value : num 66
 $ x     : chr "70-74"
 $ y     : num 66
 $ widget: chr "bars"

The input is set again on every click, also when the same item is clicked twice. Give another input name with argument inputId.

In a dashboard

Give an output item the field click.events: true: the chart returned by its service sends its clicks to input <item name>_item_click, used by the services of other items like any input. The example dashboard click-events shows a graph and a bar chart and the items clicked on them:

# Clicks on chart items as shiny inputs.
# An output with 'click.events: true' sends clicks on the items of its chart (nodes, links, bars, points, ...)
# to input <output name>_item_click: a list with the type, id, label, series, value, ... of the clicked item.
# This works for Graphviz diagrams (rvis grviz and DiagrammeR), networkD3, echarts4r, apexcharter, plotly and
# highcharter charts; see ?rvisClickEvents for other widgets.
name: Click events
layout: page

objects:
  network:
    nodes: !expr data.frame(id = c('raw', 'clean', 'model', 'report'), label = c('Raw data', 'Cleaning', 'Model', 'Report'))
    links: !expr data.frame(source = c('raw', 'clean', 'model', 'clean'), target = c('clean', 'model', 'report', 'report'))

items:
  page:
    type: fluidPage
    title: Click a node, a link or a bar
    # a row of two columns (graph and bars), then a row with the clicked items
    layout: [[[graph], [bars]], [clicked]]

  graph:
    type: grvizOutput
    height: 350px
    weight: 6
    click.events: true
    service: |
      rvisPlot(type = 'graph', plotter = 'grviz', obj = session$userData$network,
               key = 'id', label = 'label', source = 'source', target = 'target')

  bars:
    type: echarts4r::echarts4rOutput
    height: 350px
    weight: 6
    click.events: true
    service: |
      deaths <- data.frame(age = rownames(VADeaths), VADeaths, check.names = FALSE)
      rvisPlot(type = 'bar', plotter = 'echarts', obj = deaths, x = 'age', y = list('Rural Male', 'Urban Male'))

  clicked:
    type: verbatimTextOutput
    service: |
      cat('Graph:\n'); str(input$graph_item_click)
      cat('\nBars:\n'); str(input$bars_item_click)

Run it with runDashboard(rvisDashboardExample("click-events")).

What a click gives

The value of the input is a list. Field type says what was clicked, and the other fields are given as available:

Field Meaning
type "node", "link", "point" (bars, points, slices), "cell" (tables), "marker" or "shape" (maps), "element" (selector mode)
id id of the item: node key, category, row name, marker layerId, …
label text shown for the item
series series (or group) of the item
index position of the item in its series
value, x, y value and coordinates of the item
source, target ends of a link
row, column row number (as in R) and column name of a table cell
lat, lng clicked point of a map
group, depth, parent group of a node or marker, level and parent in a hierarchy
data the d3 data of the clicked element (networkD3 and selector mode)
widget id of the chart

Supported charts

Plotter (package) Clickable items Notes
grviz (DiagrammeR) and DiagrammeR::grViz() nodes, edges nodes of rvis grviz graphs are reported by their key
networkD3 nodes, links sankey, force and tree networks
echarts (echarts4r) all chart items all chart types, including graphs and sankeys
apexcharter bars, points, slices
plotly points, bars
highcharter points, bars, slices
amCharts (rAmCharts) bars, points, slices rAmCharts charts are converted to htmlwidgets by rvisClickEvents(); rAmCharts::renderAmCharts() needs library(rAmCharts)
c3, billboarder bars, points, slices found under the transparent event layer of these charts
visNetwork nodes, edges
DT table cells row, column, value, and the row name as id
dygraphs points the series nearest to the pointer; the date as the chart shows it
leaflet markers, shapes including layers added later, for example by leafletProxy()
coffeewheel (rvis) sunburst arcs name, value, depth, parent

Some packages also set inputs of their own (like input$<id>_click of DiagrammeR and billboarder, the event_data() of plotly or the _marker_click inputs of leaflet). They keep working: rvis uses its own input name, <id>_item_click, which has the same form for all charts.

Any other widget: a CSS selector

For any other htmlwidget, give the CSS selector of its clickable elements:

output$sun <- sunburstR::renderSunburst(
  rvisClickEvents(sunburstR::sunburst(sequences), selector = "path"))

The input then gets the id of the clicked element (its data-id attribute, svg title or id), its text, and its d3 data in field data. Elements under a transparent layer, or which ignore the pointer, are found too.

Good to know

  • Charts whose packages bring different versions of the d3 javascript library cannot share a page: for example coffeewheel (d3 version 3) with networkD3, or c3 with billboarder. This is a limit of the packages, not of the click events.
  • dygraphs selects a point when the pointer moves over the plot: a click without moving the pointer first gives no point.
  • A failure of the click javascript is written as a warning in the browser console and never stops the chart, or the other charts of the page, from being shown.
